080cc61596b4.en: Received-not-invoiced value is worked out for you.

dd76896e5aa0.en: Every purchase order keeps its revisions, its delivery progress and its paperwork. Suppliers accept the order and record each dispatch with a QR delivery note; your team scans it, confirms what arrived and flags anything short or damaged. Goods received, invoices and credit notes all count towards the committed and incurred cost in the report.

a5c5916255a5.en: Can I still print and email purchase orders?

e0480f38ae96.en: Yes. Each order prints as a tidy PO document or PDF and is emailed to the supplier, who can also see it in the free portal.

b986096e4b2d.en: When does an order count as committed?

0934b5317277.en: When it is sent. Drafts don't count, so you can prepare orders without changing the report. Committed cost per order is the order value or the invoices, whichever is higher.

6a9ad8967dfb.en: Yes. Record what arrived on each line, as many times as needed, or confirm a supplier's dispatch and mark anything short, damaged or wrong.

9dffe6e13a7d.en: Do suppliers need an I-Cost account?

001de93f4a41.en: They receive the order by email, and can use the free supplier portal to accept it, record dispatches and print QR delivery notes.

c44f34a5295f.en: Yes, two ways. With the live Xero connection, Send to Xero puts supplier invoices into Xero as draft bills with one click, or by themselves as each one is approved: suppliers become Xero contacts, projects become tracking, and paid dates come back to I-Cost, with an email to the supplier if you want. I-Cost never approves, pays or deletes anything in Xero. It is £10 a month for your whole company, and we switch it on when you ask from inside I-Cost. Or, free, Export bills for Xero downloads a file in Xero's bill import layout to import yourself. QuickBooks and Sage aren't supported yet.
